ConocoPhillips fell 1.7% today as oil prices retreated on signs that geopolitical tensions in the Middle East may ease. Iran's foreign minister indicated willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz—a critical global oil chokepoint—within a week and return to nuclear negotiations, which reduced the risk premium traders had been pricing into crude. US oil dropped to $96.41 per barrel, and the stock has now lost 7.4% over two weeks as these diplomatic signals have accumulated.

The broader pattern here reflects how heavily oil majors trade on supply-disruption fears: when the threat of conflict recedes, so does the price cushion that had been supporting the sector. Even though global oil remains elevated at $114.89 per barrel, the prospect of Persian Gulf stabilization removes one of the main props that kept energy stocks elevated during weeks of heightened tension.
